Subject: Clarify billing for short concurrent sessions + heartbeat floor

Hi Vanessa,

Quick one from our engineering and procurement teams. We run a user-facing assistant that opens many short-lived websocket sessions (5–20s) concurrently — typically 30–150 concurrent sessions during peak minutes. Each session sends the same 2.5k-token prefix (customer context) and then 40–120 tokens of user input per request.

Questions:
- How are the per-session minimums applied when sessions share the same prefix? Do we get prefix reuse credit across concurrent sockets or is the minimum charged per active session?
- How does the heartbeat/keepalive (we send a 1-token heartbeat every 30s) factor into flooring or microburst credits?
- Can you show a sample invoice line or two with the rounding behavior (e.g., floor to 1k token slabs, microburst credit applied)?

We need something concrete for our procurement team to approve the pilot (they asked for sample invoice lines). Any example math would be great.

Hi Sam — thanks for the clear use case.

Short answers up front:
- We credit prefix reuse across sessions when the requests are routed to the same conversation shard and KV cache is hit; that reduces billed input tokens for the repeated prefix.
- Minimums (floors) are applied per logical request stream (we count active session requests) but we apply a microburst offset that can absorb very short-lived spikes before the floor is enforced.

I'll attach a couple of example invoice lines and ask Jordan to include a worked example with your numbers (concurrency 30–150, 2.5k prefix + 40–120 user tokens). If procurement needs a one-page note we can produce it after this thread.

Sending sample invoice and a short calculation in my next message.

Sam — adding the math so procurement has something to review. I kept it conservative.

Assumptions (based on your note):
- Peak concurrency: 100 concurrent sessions (midpoint of 30–150)
- Prefix: 2500 tokens (static for each session)
- User payload per request: 80 tokens avg
- Requests per session per minute: 1.2 (interactive clicks)
- Billing quantum (example product plan): 1,000-token floor per request stream per minute; microburst credit = 500 tokens per minute before floor triggers

Example (per-minute snapshot):
- Raw tokens inbound across all sessions = (2500 + 80) * 100 = 258,000 tokens
- If KV cache is hot and prefix is reused on the same serving shard, we credit the prefix once per shard. Conservative credit: assume 10 shards serving 10 sessions each → prefix charged 10 * 2500 = 25,000 tokens instead of 250,000 → net billed input tokens = 25,000 + (80 * 100) = 33,000 tokens

Flooring & rounding:
- We evaluate floors per active logical session stream. With microburst credit of 500 tokens/min, a session sending 80 tokens would be covered by the microburst and not hit the 1,000-token floor in that minute. Only sessions that exceed the microburst + actual tokens would be rounded up to the 1,000-token slab.

Illustrative invoice lines (minute aggregated, simplified):
1) Input tokens — cached-prefix-adjusted: 33,000 tokens billed at rate X → billed units = 33 (if 1k-token quantum)
2) Microburst absorption credit applied: -50 units equivalent (applied as a negative line item)
3) Floor rounding adjustments: +8 units (multiple small sessions that exceeded microburst threshold get rounded to the 1k slab)

Net billed units (minute sample) ≈ 33 - 50 + 8 = -9 units → for short windows we apply minimum invoice aggregation logic (we never credit a negative net; negative indicates credits to be applied across invoice period). In practice, over hourly aggregation the microburst absorption smooths and you will see net positive units that match usage.

Notes / operational guardrails:
- Prefix-credit effectiveness depends on routing affinity. If sessions get routed to different shards, prefix reuse credit is reduced. We can discuss affinity pinning for your pilot.
- Heartbeat tokens (1-token every 30s) are considered minimal; for sessions that are otherwise idle they may slowly push a session over microburst threshold if run continuously. We typically recommend a 60s heartbeat for low-cost keepalive where possible.

If you want, we can run a 24-hour simulated invoice using your telemetry and a tuned routing policy (affinity vs best-effort) and produce a sample invoice by line item. That will be the most helpful for procurement.

—Jordan
